sup-70a7e22ae57de624-w2:d.ii.hint: Use the amplitude to fix the total energy, then compare the position with equilibrium.
notes: For SHM, v² = ω²(A² − x²), and total energy is ½mω²A². The kinetic energy depends on how far the oscillator is from equilibrium.
At a turning point speed is zero; at equilibrium its magnitude is ωA. Doubling amplitude changes total energy by a factor of four, not two.

sup-70a7e22ae57de624-w9:a.hint: Compare the particle’s displacement direction with the direction in which the wave travels.
notes: Transverse waves have particle oscillations perpendicular to propagation; longitudinal waves have them parallel. Energy travels even though particles oscillate locally.
For a moving wave profile, use a slightly later snapshot to infer the particle’s next displacement. Do not assume a particle moves along the plotted curve.

sup-70a7e22ae57de624-w9:b.i.hint: Check whether the question compares amplitude, intensity, or total power; these do not scale in the same way.
notes: For the same medium and frequency, intensity is proportional to amplitude squared. For an isotropic point source, I = P/(4πr²).
When coherent waves overlap, add their signed displacements first and then square the resultant amplitude. Adding intensities alone loses the interference effect.
